labels.readBy: primary annotator; all 12 read in full (recital + reasons)

feasibility.pairingAtJudgmentLevel: YES, 12 of 12. The party's cited articles and the court's reasons are both identifiable and comparable.
feasibility.pairingAtPropositionLevel: NO. The court almost never names the party's article in order to reject it -- it simply reasons elsewhere. Without the court naming it, ADOPT-vs-REJECT-vs-BYPASS cannot be separated by reading, because there is nothing to read.
feasibility.consequence: The six-way taxonomy is NOT codeable on this corpus. It collapses to three codes that are.

C00.note: party invoked Evidence 35 to compel production; court decided the claimant's own evidence insufficient, on CCL 16 and Evidence 96

C01.note: defendant absent; court decided on default under Sharia 57

C02.note: court reached the substance through Evidence 29

C03.note: party invoked Evidence 34; court found the relationship from the defendant's self-contradiction and Evidence 29

C05.note: court adopts the party's Arbitration 11 and adds Arbitration 5. IMPORTANT: the layer recorded only art 5 for the court, because art 11 was cited as «في مادته المادة الحادية عشرة» -- an instrument-first possessive form. Measured engagement is therefore a LOWER bound.

C06.note: parties settled; court recorded the settlement under Sharia 70

C08.note: claim paid and withdrawn under Sharia 92

C09.note: party cited four articles across two codes; court appointed an expert under Evidence 110

C10.note: court addressed the party's forgery allegation, but through art 55 of the Evidence procedural manual rather than the articles pleaded

C11.note: court adopts Evidence 29 and adds four structural articles

labels.verdict: In 8 of 12, the court answered on law the party had not cited. In 2 it engaged the party's own article and added to it. In 2 the dispute was mooted before the law mattered. The pattern is consistent with the article-level overlap figures and is a pilot, not an estimate.
